items.context: GCT has no GitHub SDK in go.mod today. The choice locks the surface area of GitHubClient and the test seam. go-github/v66 has full REST coverage (PRs, releases, tags, branches), WithEnterpriseURLs() for GHE, and the standard interface-wrap + httptest mocking pattern. cli/go-gh is thinner and assumes a gh-auth session, which conflicts with reusing the encrypted credential store. Hand-rolled costs an integration tax per endpoint.

options.label: github.com/google/go-github/v66 wrapped behind a narrow GitHubClient interface
options.rationale: Full REST coverage, Enterprise URL support, idiomatic mocking. Lowest implementation risk for PR + release surface together.

options.label: github.com/cli/go-gh/v2
options.rationale: Smaller dependency footprint, but assumes an external gh auth session and provides less typed coverage.

options.label: Hand-rolled net/http client
options.rationale: Maximum control, no transitive deps; pays an integration tax per endpoint and reinvents pagination/rate-limit handling.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own preference (e.g. license/vendoring constraints).

items.context: SSH stays the transport for git push/pull. The GitHub *API* needs token auth. Today CredentialTypeHTTPS already stores user+token in an AES-256-GCM-encrypted file (api/credentials_store.go:53,170-189). The question is which auth modes V1 supports.

options.label: GitHub PAT only in V1; defer GitHub App to a follow-up
options.rationale: Matches single-user CLI/dev posture, reuses credential store with a small `service` tag, no new flows. Lowest scope.

options.label: PAT + GitHub App (installation tokens) in V1
options.rationale: Future-proof for multi-user/shared deployments but adds JWT signing, key storage, and installation-id resolution to the V1 surface.

options.label: Reuse SSH key for API too (e.g. via deploy keys / GitHub SSH-based auth)
options.rationale: Avoids token storage but GitHub's REST/GraphQL API does not authenticate via SSH keys; this option is effectively infeasible and is here to be ruled out.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Specify a different posture (e.g. fine-grained PAT only, or App-only).

items.context: ReviewDimensions (api/review_model.go:29-45) gives structured code-quality, tests, standards, visual, provenance data plus a green/yellow/red readiness signal. We can render this directly, or wrap it in an LLM, or both.

options.label: Deterministic Markdown template fed by ReviewDimensions; LLM polish deferred
options.rationale: Predictable, testable with zero external calls, matches commit-message-AI being a P1 add-on rather than gating P0.

options.label: Template + optional LLM polish behind a flag in V1
options.rationale: Better prose immediately but adds a provider abstraction and another mock surface to V1.

options.label: LLM-only generation from raw review payload
options.rationale: Most natural-sounding output; least testable, hardest to make deterministic, depends on review data quality.

items.topic: Scope: should this research also lock the release/tag API design?
items.context: Two execute siblings depend on this research and share the client + auth + mock decisions: execute/gct-github-pr-api and execute/gct-github-release-api. Splitting research duplicates the auth/mock decisions; bundling keeps them aligned.

options.label: Bundle: this research locks the shared client/auth/mock design and lets each execute item own its endpoint shape
options.rationale: Single source of truth for the shared surface; lower coordination cost.

options.label: Split: this research covers PRs only; spin up a separate research for releases/tags
options.rationale: Smaller individual scope but redoes the auth/library/mock conversation.

items.text: GCT credentials already supports GitHub PATs without a new type: CredentialTypeHTTPS (api/credentials_model.go:10) is username+token, AES-256-GCM-encrypted at ~/.config/git-control-tower/credentials.enc (api/credentials_store.go:53). The V1 extension is a 'service' or 'provider' tag so a GitHub API token can be stored independently of remote-URL-bound git HTTPS credentials.

The repo's mock convention is hand-rolled fakes in *_fake_test.go with error-injection fields and in-memory state (see git_runner_fake_test.go, audit_logger_fake_test.go). FakeGitHubClient should follow the same shape — no mockgen, no gomock — and live in github_client_fake_test.go.

Review data is already PR-description-ready. ReviewDimensions (api/review_model.go:29-45) carries code-quality score+top issues, test pass/fail counts+failures, standards violations with file/line/severity, visual screenshots, provenance — plus review_readiness.go gives a green/yellow/red label. A deterministic Markdown template can compose these into a structured PR body without an LLM.

go.mod has no GitHub SDK today (only google/uuid, gorilla/mux, gorilla/handlers, vrooli/api-core, vrooli/repo-contract-go, golang.org/x/sync, modernc.org/sqlite). Whichever library wins d1, this is a new dependency the team takes on for this initiative.

Existing remote auth path (git_runner.go gitCredentialEnv) already injects HTTPS user/password via GIT_USERNAME/GIT_PASSWORD/GIT_ASKPASS for git transport. The GitHub *API* path is fully separate from this — it uses Bearer auth on REST/GraphQL — so V1 work does not need to touch the git-transport credential plumbing.
